headline: Vermont education agency unveils 2026-2030 plan built around four statewide priorities
dek: The Agency of Education says the plan will guide work on college and career readiness, academic achievement, school climate and agency operations through 2030.
body: Vermont’s Agency of Education has released a 2026-2030 strategic plan that sets a statewide direction for public education and lays out how the agency says it will measure progress. The plan was published Oct. 1 after nearly two years of input from educators, students, families, school and district leaders and community partners, according to the [Agency of Education’s announcement](https://education.vermont.gov/press-release/vermont-agency-education-releases-statewide-strategic-plan) and a report by [Vermont Business Magazine](https://vermontbiz.com/news/2026/october/01/vermont-agency-education-releases-statewide-strategic-plan).

The document arrives as Vermont schools and state officials confront pressures that the agency identifies as declining enrollment, changing demographics, workforce strain and shifting expectations for graduates. Those are statewide conditions rather than a promise that the plan will solve any one district’s budget or staffing problem. The agency describes its role as providing leadership, setting expectations, supporting schools and maintaining transparency and accountability for results.

The plan organizes that work under four connected pillars. College and Career Readiness is intended to help students leave school with the knowledge, skills and experiences needed for what comes next. Academic Excellence for All focuses on teaching, meaningful learning and more equitable outcomes. Safe and Healthy Schools covers the conditions that help students belong, engage and learn. Operational Effectiveness addresses the systems, data and capacity behind the agency’s work, according to the agency’s [strategic-plan webpage](https://education.vermont.gov/about/strategic-plan).

The priorities are broad by design, but the agency says they will be translated into annual work. Each year, officials plan to set priorities, identify milestones, measure progress and report on what they learn. The agency’s webpage also links to a 2026-27 implementation plan and a 2025-26 progress report, creating a structure for comparing the long-range goals with specific near-term actions.

The plan’s development timeline shows how the agency assembled that framework. During a 2024 Listen and Learn Tour, the agency says it heard from more than 1,000 education leaders, educators, parents, students and community members across Vermont. In November 2025, it hosted more than 300 educators and other partners at a strategic-planning retreat. During 2026, participants from around the state met through steering committees to develop strategies tied to the agency’s vision.

That process matters because the plan is not a new school-funding formula or a single mandate for local districts. It is an operating framework for the state agency, which oversees and supports Vermont’s public education system while schools continue to make local decisions. Its effect will depend on how the agency turns the four pillars into guidance, technical support, data reporting and decisions about where to direct its limited capacity.

The agency’s announcement says the plan is meant to evolve as implementation produces new information. That gives the document a built-in review cycle, but it also leaves important questions for later reports: which student outcomes will be used as benchmarks, how milestones will be measured across districts with different circumstances, and whether the agency’s annual priorities match the needs heard during the public-input process.

For now, the next step is the 2026-27 implementation plan and the reporting that follows it. Vermont’s education agency says it will continue working with educators, families, students and community partners as the strategy moves from a published framework to yearly commitments. The plan’s value will ultimately be judged less by its four headings than by whether those commitments produce clearer support and better outcomes for students across the state.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Vermont education agency releases 2026-2030 strategic plan
seoDescription: Vermont’s Agency of Education released a 2026-2030 strategic plan centered on four statewide public-education priorities.
